newsitem.title: POLAND: Hachette group sole bidder for Ruch - Kwasniewski.
newsitem.headline: Hachette group sole bidder for Ruch - Kwasniewski.

text.p: President Aleksander Kwasniewski offered encouragement on Friday to French investors and notably to a group led by France's Hachette press distributor which is bidding to buy Poland's major news-stand chain Ruch SA.

Briefing foreign journalists before next week's visit to Poland by French President Jacques Chirac, Kwasniewski stressed his country wanted French investment as part of its drive to achieve greater balance in its foreign economic relations.
"I want to assure, from a political point of view... that Poland is very interested in the presence of French capital on the Polish market," Kwasniewski said. @
Kwasniewski dismissed an announcement this week by a nascent Polish consortium that it planned to rival the Hachette group's bid for state-owned Ruch.

"No other formal offer can now come in because it is already too late, but negotiations continue with Hachette on the eventual agreement," said Kwasniewski, adding that the new consortium did not yet even formally exist.
He stressed that he was not a partner in negotiations himself and all such deals had to undergo accepted procedures. @

An informal group, including private television channel Polsat, mineral water producer Multico and the operator of Poland's lottery said on Tuesday it had written to the privatisation minister to make an offer for Ruch.
It aimed to acquire 40 percent of Ruch, with 40 percent offered to the public and the treasury retaining 20 percent.
It said Bank Rozwoju Exportu SA (BRE) was also involved but a bank spokesman later declined to confirm this.
Zycie Warszawy newspaper, published by Multico, said on the consortium would offer about $120 million for Ruch.
Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz was quoted by PAP news agency as saying the bid was "considerably better" than that from Hachette, which he called unreasonably low.
Hachette, Polish publisher group UWP and other firms are seeking more than 50 percent of Ruch and Chirac is likely to back them.
News-stand chain Ruch, which controls about 65 percent of Poland's press distribution market, had a net profit of 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys in 1995.
It has about 17,000 news-stands and was the country's sole press distributor before the 1989 fall of communism.
Kwasniewski said diversifying investment and trade partners was a priority for Poland although it appreciated the role of Germany which accounted for 38 percent of its total trade.
"We can and will use this visit (by Chirac)... to strengthen economic and trade ties with France," he said.

One tough issue is that of telecommunications company France Telecom, a partner in a Polish firm which has not received a licence to operate a new digital GSM telephone network, despite an promise from a previous government.
"I think we will raise the subject of France Telecom, although it is most complicated," Kwasniewski said.
